title: Large Language Models for Tumor Board Decision Making
summary:
Lung cancer is a very serious disease. Doctors from various specialties discuss in joint meetings (tumor boards) which treatment is best for each patient – ​​e.g., surgery, medication, radiation, or a combination.

New artificial intelligence can very effectively analyze medical texts and findings and could assist doctors in this process. Initial studies show promising results.

Research Question
We want to find out whether the artificial intelligence's suggestions for lung cancer patients are as effective as the actual decisions made by the doctors. We also examine its strengths and areas for improvement.

Methodology
We are retrospectively analyzing the data of 50 real patients with lung cancer. The artificial intelligence receives the same information as the doctors and makes its own suggestions. We compare these anonymously with the actual decisions made by the doctors. In this way, we measure similarities and differences. The study uses only existing, anonymized data and does not burden anyone with new information.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of therapeutic agreement between computer-generated suggestions and multidisciplinary tumor board decisions in patients from 2021 to 2026

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Data analysis of patients who were in treatment between 2021 and 2026
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion of all cases without a full board decision, without sufficient imaging findings, or with incomplete documentation of the relevant routine data.
